title: How the $299 Robot Mop Dock Actually Cleans Itself
description: Wondering how a $299 robot vacuum mop washes its own mop pads? I broke down the exact dock cycle: hot water wash, roller wringing, warm-air drying, and auto-empty dustbin rated for 4-7 weeks. I also flag the one failure point reviewers mention most — underpowered drying that leads to sour-smelling mop pads within weeks. If you're comparing wet-dry combos this Black Friday, this is the mechanism worth understanding before you spend $299.

title: Pet Owners: What $299 Robot Vacuum Mops Still Miss
description: Before you buy a $299 robot vacuum mop for pet hair, read what reviewers with pets actually report. The real complaint isn't suction — it's roller brush tangling with long hair and mop pads dragging hair at carpet transitions. Short pet hair on hard floors is handled well; long-haired dogs and cats on area rugs still need manual cleanup. I cover the $5.99 tool that covers the baseboards and litter box edges a robot's edge brush can't reach.

title: The Hidden Yearly Cost of a $299 Robot Vacuum Mop
description: A $299 robot vacuum mop isn't actually $299 a year. I calculated the real maintenance cost: mop pads wear out every 3-6 months, dustbin bags need swapping on a kitchen-trash cadence, and dock-cleaning solution is an ongoing line item. Budget an extra $15-$20 a quarter for consumables — I found the specific $5.99-$13.32 products that cover bags, pads, and cleaning solution without surprise mid-swap failures. Full cost breakdown and product picks in the post.
